raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging", "note": "They are trying to figure out if they fit in your story, if your family is a safe place to bring hard truths" },
  "read": "Your kid is at the stage where they are actively constructing who they are, and they are using you as a reference point. When they asked that question they were not trying to catch you out, they were trying to see if you are a real person they can learn from, not just a rule-giver. Your freeze sent a signal, even if you did not mean it to: either this topic is off-limits, or adults do not have to be honest. Both readings chip away at your credibility exactly when they need you most.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Keep deflecting or change the subject to protect yourself from discomfort, which leaves them with the silence and teaches them that honesty with you has a ceiling" },
  "mentorMove": "Go back and open the door yourself, before they stop knocking. A short, honest answer that names what you actually did and what it cost you is more powerful than any lecture you could ever give, because it treats them as someone mature enough to handle real information.",
  "holdFirm": ["They deserve a real answer, not a sanitized one or a non-answer dressed up as wisdom", "Your honesty is the standard, not optional warmth you can skip when it is inconvenient for you"],
  "stayFlexible": ["How much detail you share is yours to calibrate based on their age and what is actually useful to them", "You can answer in one conversation or open it up over a few, as long as you actually open it"],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, can we circle back to what you asked me the other day? I froze up and I want to be straight with you about why, and then actually answer you." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Before I do, can I ask what made you bring it up? I want to make sure I am answering what you were actually wondering, not just what I assume you meant." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what actually happened when I was around your age. [Give the honest version, proportionate to their maturity.] I am not proud of all of it, and I do not want to spin it into a lesson before you have even had a chance to react. What do you think about that?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I want you to be able to ask me anything, and I want to give you real answers, not performances. That is a high bar and I am going to hold myself to it, because I think you are old enough and smart enough to handle the truth, and honestly you deserve it from me more than anyone." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Every time you go back and repair a freeze or a dodge, you build the kind of relationship where they bring you the genuinely hard stuff before it becomes a crisis. The goal is not to be the cool parent who confesses everything, it is to be the honest one they trust enough to actually talk to when it matters."
}
situation: My teenager asked me a hard question about something I did at their age, and I froze instead of answering.
